action.action-desc: Mr. Rulli (for himself, Mr. Bentz, Mr. Carter of Georgia, Mrs. Fischbach, Mr. Taylor, and Mr. Biggs of Arizona) introduced the following bill; which was referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce

form.official-title: To amend title XIX of the Social Security Act to require States to conduct fraud risk assessments under the Medicaid program.

section.text: This Act may be cited as the Medicaid Fraud Prevention Act.
Section 1902 of the Social Security Act (42 U.S.C. 1396a) is amended—

subparagraph.text: in paragraph (89), by striking and at the end;
in paragraph (90), by striking the period at the end and inserting ; and; and
by inserting after paragraph (90) the following new paragraph:

paragraph.text: provide that the State shall comply with the fraud risk assessment requirements under subsection (zz).
by adding at the end the following new subsection:
For purposes of subsection (a)(91), the fraud risk assessment requirements under this subsection are that the State shall—

subparagraph.text: not later than 1 year after the date of the enactment of this subsection and not less frequently than annually thereafter, complete a fraud risk assessment as described in paragraph (2);

not later than 90 days after completing such an assessment, implement a corrective action plan to address any vulnerabilities identified in such assessment that includes measurable outcomes and specific deadlines with respect to the completion of corrective actions under such plan; and

not later than 1 year after the completion of the first fraud risk assessment under this subsection, and annually thereafter, submit to the Secretary a report that includes the information specified in paragraph (3) with respect to the preceding year.

For purposes of paragraph (1), a fraud risk assessment described in this paragraph is a comprehensive assessment of fraud risks across all components of the State plan (and any waiver of such plan), including with respect to medical assistance provided on a fee-for-service basis, medical assistance provided through a managed care entity, and eligibility determination and enrollment systems (including systems operated by or on behalf of the State for the purposes of eligibility verification and redetermination) under such plan (or waiver), that—

clause.text: to the extent practicable, uses data from existing Federal and State program integrity systems, including—

subclause.text: the Payment Error Rate Measurement program (or any successor program);
the Transformed Medicaid Statistical Information System (or any successor system);
data from a State medicaid fraud control unit (as defined in section 1903(q)) or another program integrity activity;
the Public Assistance Reporting Information System (PARIS) (or any successor system); and
beginning October 1, 2029, the system established by the Secretary under subsection (uu);

clause.text: identifies and ranks the most significant fraud, waste, and abuse vulnerabilities of such plan (or waiver);

estimates the amount that could potentially be improperly expended under such plan (or waiver) due to each such vulnerability, including any improper payments associated with each such vulnerability, with respect to, at minimum, the 12-month period beginning on the date on which such assessment is completed;
evaluates the effectiveness of existing program integrity tools under such plan (or waiver);
identifies gaps in data sharing, oversight, and enforcement with respect to fraud, waste, and abuse under such plan (or waiver); and
follows the guidelines established by the Secretary under subparagraph (B).

subparagraph.text: Not later than January 1, 2027, the Secretary shall establish guidelines that—

clause.text: identify and define standardized categories of fraud, waste, and abuse risk across State plans (and waivers of such plans), including with respect to eligibility determinations, provider enrollments, claims processing, and managed care;

establish criteria for the identification, scoring, and prioritization of categories of risk identified under clause (i) on the basis of the likelihood of such risks and estimates of potential improper expenditures (as described in subparagraph (A)(iii)) due to such risks; and
enable fraud risk assessments completed under this subsection by different States to be effectively compared.

paragraph.text: For purposes of paragraph (1), the information specified in this paragraph is—

subparagraph.text: the results of any fraud risk assessments conducted under paragraph (1)(A);
the most significant fraud, waste, and abuse vulnerabilities identified under such assessments;
the potential improper expenditures (as described in paragraph (2)(A)(iii)) estimated under such assessments;
corrective actions taken or planned to be taken under paragraph (1)(B) with respect to such vulnerabilities; and
an explanation of any progress made in addressing such vulnerabilities.

paragraph.text: Not later than 1 year after the date on which the first report under paragraph (1)(C) is submitted to the Secretary, and annually thereafter, the Secretary shall submit to Congress a report that, with respect to the preceding year—

subparagraph.text: analyzes the findings from reports submitted to the Secretary under such paragraph;
identifies national trends with respect to Medicaid fraud risk;
evaluates State implementation of corrective action plans implemented under paragraph (1)(B); and
includes recommendations for legislative or administrative action to address fraud, waste, and abuse vulnerabilities identified in such reports.
